stories.headline: Supreme Court Asks MEA To Issue Public Notice Inviting Compensation Claims From Families Of Indians Killed In Russia-Ukraine War
stories.title: Supreme Court Asks MEA To Issue Public Notice Inviting Compensation Claims From Families Of Indians Killed In Russia-Ukraine War
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Wednesday asked the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) to issue a public notice inviting compensation claims from families of Indian nationals who died while fighting in the Russia-Ukraine war as part of the Russian armed forces, noting that only six families had sought compensation despite 51 reported deaths.
A bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi directed the MEA to provide assistance to the affected families in securing compensation from Russian authorities.
The Court also asked the Ministry to place on record the compensation amounts determined by the Russian authorities and the amounts actually paid to the families.
“It is obvious that the right to seek compensation needs to be apprised to the other family members of the victims.
We are informed that the MEA is contacting those families one by one to secure the necessary documents and information.
It might be advisable for the MEA to issue a public notice and invite claims and thereafter provide full assistance to those families in order to secure the compensatory benefits for them.
In this regard, we expect that if fresh status report we find by the MEA”, the Court observed.

The Court passed the order in a writ petition filed by family members of 26 Indian nationals who allegedly travelled to Russia in search of employment but were recruited into the Russian armed forces.
The petition raises allegations of deception and human trafficking in connection with the recruitment of Indians to fight in the Russia-Ukraine war.
On July 31, 2026, the Supreme Court directed the MEA to appoint a nodal officer to coordinate with the families of deceased and injured Indian nationals who had travelled to Russia.

The Court also directed the Ministry to arrange DNA tests to identify mortal remains, provide families with the procedure and documents required to claim compensation from Russian authorities, and ensure that pending compensation claims did not delay the handover of mortal remains.
It further directed the Legal Services.

With four manufacturing units, 11 warehouses, more than 153 employees and over 100 customers, the company has established a scalable operating footprint across India’s key industrial corridors.
Its integrated portfolio spans returnable transport packaging, rental pooling, expendable packaging, onsite packaging with automation, reverse logistics, asset management and transportation.
This integrated model enables customers to reduce capital intensity, improve asset productivity and build more resilient supply chains.
Its strength lies in an asset-light, consultative and technology-enabled approach that combines engineering capabilities with operational execution and recurring-service opportunities.

As manufacturers increasingly prioritise cost optimisation, traceability and circularity, Vevra is positioning itself to capture this shift with a platform designed for scale, recurring revenue and long-term customer integration.
Its proposition extends beyond packaging to the continuous optimisation of the supply chain itself.

Recognising the transformative potential of the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM) amid the post-pandemic digital shift, he founded.
One SG Technologies in 2024.
The company believes that India needs a patient-centric and interoperable care ecosystem and is working to bridge gaps in connected healthcare through its flagship interoperability platform, OneHCX®.

A key focus is addressing the complexity and unpredictability of medical claim outcomes, particularly against the backdrop of inadequate health coverage and the resulting friction between payers and providers.

stories.headline: Cabinet clears ₹53,428 cr. for social assistance programme till 2030-31, drops ‘Indira Gandhi’ from pension scheme names
stories.title: Cabinet clears ₹53,428 cr. for social assistance programme till 2030-31, drops ‘Indira Gandhi’ from pension scheme names
stories.summary: Critics question fixed five-year allocation for social pensions, saying it fails to account for rising beneficiary numbers and inflation
reasons: source: event has 2 copies, primary source counted once
corroboration: 2 independent source groups -> high confidence
event term: 'cabinet clears' in title weight 44
candidate gate: no category but HIGH+ priority -> allowed
article_sentences: The Union Cabinet on Wednesday (October 14, 2026) approved an outlay of ₹53,428 crore for the continuation of the National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP) for five years, from 2026-27 to 2030-31, with revised eligibility criteria and assistance rates for disability pension beneficiaries.
The scheme will be renamed the 'Pradhan Mantri Samajik Sahayata Yojana', while its pension and family benefit components will also be renamed, according to an official statement.
Under the revised norms, monthly assistance under the disability pension scheme will be ₹375 for beneficiaries aged up to 79 years and ₹625 for those aged 80 years and above.
The benchmark disability requirement for availing of the pension has been reduced from 80% to 40%.
The minimum age criterion has also been removed, making persons with disabilities eligible for assistance from birth.

The revised eligibility criteria, beneficiary coverage and assistance rates under the disability pension scheme will be implemented within three months of the issuance of guidelines, the statement read.
The pension schemes for the elderly and widows, along with the National Family Benefit Scheme, will continue in their existing form.
The Cabinet's approval is expected to benefit 3.20 crore beneficiaries across all 36 States and Union territories.

The Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme will be renamed the 'Pradhan Mantri Vridhavastha Pension Yojana', while the Indira Gandhi National Widow Pension Scheme will be called the 'Pradhan Mantri Vidhawa Pension Yojana'.

The Indira Gandhi National Disability Pension Scheme will be renamed the 'Pradhan Mantri Divyangjan Pension Yojana', and the National Family Benefit Scheme will become the 'Pradhan Mantri Parivar Labh Yojana'.
Launched on August 15, 1995, the NSAP provides assistance to poor households as part of the Centre's responsibility under Article 41 of the Directive Principles of State Policy in the Constitution.
The Centre provides 100% central assistance under the programme to ensure uniform availability of support to beneficiaries across the country.

stories.title: Centre says CAPF Act does not overrule Supreme Court IPS deputation order
stories.summary: Centre says CAPF Act does not overrule Supreme Court IPS deputation order

article_sentences: The Centre defended the CAPF Act before the Supreme Court against a challenge by cadre officers.
The dispute concerns IPS deputation quotas and stalled promotion opportunities within five forces.
The Centre has told the Supreme Court that the CAPFs (General Administration) Act, 2026, does not overrule its 2025 judgment directing a gradual reduction in Indian.
Police Service postings to five Central Armed.
Police Forces up to the inspector general rank.
In a joint affidavit, the Ministry of Home Affairs, the Department of Personnel and Training and the Central Reserve.
Police Force said the law was a permissible measure that changed the legal basis of the court's directions.
They sought the dismissal of a petition filed by CAPF cadre officers challenging the Act.
The petition was filed by a group of officers led by CRPF Assistant Commandant and Shaurya Chakra awardee Bibhor Kumar Singh.
They argued that the law was enacted to overrule the Supreme Court's May 2025 judgment and was arbitrary and discriminatory.
They said it did not address stagnation in the promotion of cadre officers caused by IPS officers joining the forces on deputation.
Under the Act, 50 per cent of inspector general posts are to be filled through deputation from the IPS.

stories.title: Owaisi moves Supreme Court on SIR, seeks anti-BJP alliance in Uttar Pradesh
stories.summary: Owaisi moves Supreme Court on SIR, seeks anti-BJP alliance in Uttar Pradesh

event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44

article_sentences: AIMIM has challenged the SIR process in the Supreme Court while pursuing an opposition alliance in Uttar Pradesh.
Owaisi says both efforts are crucial to protect voting rights and prevent another BJP government.

AIMIM president Asaduddin Owaisi on Wednesday said his party had filed a petition and a review petition in the Supreme Court over the SIR process, questioning whether the Election Commission's decisions were unanimous and whether statutory forms had been changed.
Owaisi also said AIMIM was pursuing alliances ahead of next year's Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections to prevent the BJP from returning to power for a third term.
He also spoke about protests against SIR, Starlink's satellite communication services and the removal of Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site.
Owaisi said the Election Commission was required by law to work collectively, but it was not known whether its decisions were unanimous or whether any member had dissented.
"We filed the review petition also because the Supreme Court upheld SIR.
We were petitioners in the Bihar SIR case.
It is not understood whether the statutory form for enumeration has been changed.
We don't have any material.
We filed a detailed petition in the Supreme Court," he told reporters.
He said no other party in Telangana had matched AIMIM's efforts during the SIR process over the past three months.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Must Revisit Verdict Upholding SIR: Justice Abhay Oka
stories.title: Supreme Court Must Revisit Verdict Upholding SIR: Justice Abhay Oka
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: Supreme Court must rethink its May 2026 judgment upholding the constitutionality of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process, particularly when the process permits deletion of voters merely for not submitting the pre-filled enumeration forms, said former apex court judge Justice Abhay Oka.
"On this very ground itself, the Supreme Court must revisit its judgment...
The law clearly says that there can either be an intensive revision or a partial one...
Even for intensive revision under section 21(3), the law says that revision can be done only of a given constituency at one time and not all the constituencies simultaneously...
It also says that the revision must be done prior to general elections," Justice Oka said.
Another reason for revisiting this judgment is the enumeration form, which has been brought into existence by the Election Commission of India (ECI), without any power.
"The guidelines issued by the ECI says if someone doesn't fill the enumeration form, then their names will be deleted from the draft list...
This, according to me, is illegal...
This isn't a provision even under the Act of 1950 or even the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960.
A person must be removed from the list as per the law only...
And the law says, one can be removed only under section 21, which permits issuing a show cause notice to a voter and then after giving a hearing, deciding the case," Justice Oka said.
Justice Oka said that the enumeration form is not as per law and thus, if voters do not fill the same, their names cannot be deleted from the list.

stories.headline: Cabinet approves new industrial policy with focus on non-polluting sectors
stories.title: Cabinet approves new industrial policy with focus on non-polluting sectors
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'cabinet approves' in title weight 44
candidate gate: no category but HIGH+ priority -> allowed
article_sentences: The Delhi government has approved a new industrial policy that outlines a ten-year roadmap for developing a clean, knowledge-based industrial economy in the Capital, with a focus on high-value, non-polluting sectors, according to a statement from the Chief Minister’s Office (CMO) said on Wednesday.

The Industrial Policy, 2026, approved in a Cabinet meeting chaired by Chief Minister Rekha Gupta, also allocated Rs 1,000 crore under Mukhyamantri Udyamshree Yojana for five years to promote new industries and create jobs, said the statement.

Under the new policy, special incentives will be given for 10 priority sectors, including Information Technology (IT), global capability centres, data centres, healthcare, research and modern manufacturing, as per the CMO.
“Women-led micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) will receive additional support for business modernisation and expansion.
Employers hiring women will receive higher incentives for each woman recruited.
Women and young people will also receive special attention under skill development programmes.
These provisions aim to expand business and employment opportunities for women entrepreneurs and employees,” said the statement.
Ms. Gupta said the policy focuses on making better use of the Capital’s economic potential by encouraging advanced technology, research, specialised services and high-value-added industries.

“Over the next 10 years, it aims to create an investment-friendly environment, provide necessary support to entrepreneurs, promote women-led enterprises and generate new employment opportunities for young people.
It will also seek to steer Delhi’s industrial economy towards a more modern, cleaner and knowledge-based model,” she said.

Ms. Gupta said that considering the needs of different sectors, tailored incentives would be provided for capital investment, office or workspace rentals, new hiring, research, certification, technological modernisation, energy conservation and skill development.
The policy will also encourage resource reuse and waste reduction, she added.

stories.headline: Supreme Court mandates insurance on offline railway tickets from October 27
stories.title: Supreme Court mandates insurance on offline railway tickets from October 27
stories.summary: ‘At present, only persons purchasing tickets online are provided the benefit of insurance coverage upon payment of a nominal additional amount’
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court has issued a mandatory directive that tickets sold across counters at every railway station nationwide must include travel insurance coverage identical to online bookings.
A Bench of Justices Ahsanuddin Amanullah and R. Mahadevan directed the railway authorities to put the order into effect from October 27, 2026.
The order explicitly warned that failure to implement this mechanism would place direct liability squarely on the Railway Board.
“At present, only people purchasing tickets online are provided the benefit of insurance coverage upon payment of a nominal additional amount.

The court had granted sufficient time to the authorities to devise a mechanism extending such coverage to persons belonging to the lowest strata of society, who, in most cases, purchase their tickets at the railway reservation counters while undertaking journeys by train,” the court observed, pointing out that the railway had made no progress on providing insurance cover to all passengers.
The direction was based on a writ petition filed in the aftermath of the June 2023 Odisha train accident.
The petition initially focused on an independent probe into the accident and the implementation of safety systems like Kavach.

However, the court widened the scope of the case to include various passenger and infrastructural aspects of rail travel, including the lack of insurance for economically disadvantaged passengers who purchase tickets over the counter at stations.

The court, in its order dated October 6, recorded its “utter disappointment and displeasure at the conduct of the officers of the Ministry of Railways in such a serious matter concerning the safety of the common man”.
“The Railways have been representing before this court that all necessary steps are being taken in this regard.
However, it appears that such assurances have remained largely on paper and that no substantial change has taken place on the ground,” the court noted.
In a scathing order, the bench said even the budgetary provisions for the targeted areas relating to the safety of the common man and the prevention of untoward incidents had not been fully utilised.

stories.title: Cabinet approves ₹2,010 cr bonus for over 11 lakh railway employees
stories.summary: The payment of PLB, which is disbursed each year before the Durga Puja/Dusshera holidays, acts as an incentive to motivate the railway employees
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'cabinet approves' in title weight 44
candidate gate: no category but HIGH+ priority -> allowed
article_sentences: Ahead of Dussehra and Deepavali festivals, the Union Cabinet on Wednesday approved Productivity Linked Bonus of 78 days for 11,40,770 railway employees, amounting to ₹2009.61 crore.

The payment of PLB, which is disbursed each year before the Durga Puja/Dusshera holidays, acts as an incentive to motivate the railway employees for working towards improvement in the performance of the Railways, the government said.
“The maximum amount payable per eligible railway employee is ₹17,951 for 78 days,” it added.

The bonus will be paid to various categories of Railway staff like track maintainers, loco pilots, train managers (Guards), station masters, supervisors, technicians, technician helpers, pointsmen, ministerial staff and other Group C staff.
“The performance of Railways in the year 2025-26 was very good.
Railways loaded a record cargo of 1670 million tonnes and carried nearly 7.41 billion Passengers,” it said.

stories.headline: IMD to expand radar network, strengthen existing ones
stories.title: IMD to expand radar network, strengthen existing ones
stories.summary: Chennai radar was indigenously renovated in 2022, and its functioning is being closely monitored as it would help in cyclone detection
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) is looking to strengthen its existing radar network alongside installing new radars to improve weather observations and track monsoons.
With the onset of Northeast monsoon on Thursday, the IMD’s Regional Meteorological Centre is maintaining the nearly 24-year-old Chennai’s-band doppler weather radar in working condition.
It is likely to be replaced with a new S-band radar by 2027.
Installed as India’s first doppler weather radar in 2002, Chennai’s radar on Rajaji Salai continues to monitor weather up to 400 km.
Officials of the RMC said orders have been placed to replace various radars, including Chennai, Karaikal, Kolkata and Machilipatnam about six months ago.
The supplier is awaiting a component from abroad before assembling the new equipment.
In 2022, Chennai radar was indigenously renovated and its functioning is being closely monitored as it would help in cyclone detection.
Four new S-Band and X-band radars would be installed at Kanniyakumari, Tiruchi, Yercaud and Ramanathapuram under the Mission Mausam.
Radars are being installed across the country in coordination with the respective State governments.
X band radars, which have a weather surveillance range of up to 180 km, would provide accurate observations of extreme weather events, said Sivananda Damodara Pai, Head, RMC.

Mrutyunjay Mohapatra, IMD Director General, said besides the existing weather radars in places like Sriharikota, Pallikaranai, Karaikal and Chennai Rajaji Salai, new radars would cover more areas for weather observations.
Radars being maintained in the neighbouring States also help in Tamil Nadu’s weather surveillance.
